title: Order lifecycle and rider assignment
idea: A food order moves through a lifecycle where each step has an owner. Rider assignment runs beside it, offering the order to nearby riders.

analogy.text: A parcel tracking sheet: the shop signs "packed", the courier signs "collected" and "delivered". Nobody may sign another person's line.
analogy.breaks: Paper cannot refuse a wrong signature; your transition table can.

points: Each `Transition` names from, to and actor; anything not in the table is rejected.
Start rider search when the restaurant accepts, so the rider arrives near ready time.
Offer the order to the nearest riders, capped; a decline passes to the next.
No rider found is normal: queue the order and retry, never block the kitchen.

hero.title: From accepted order to reserved rider

messages.label: place O-7
messages.note: The order starts in `PLACED`. Only the restaurant or the customer can move it now.

messages.label: new order O-7
messages.note: The restaurant sees the order and decides: accept or reject.

messages.label: RESTAURANT: ACCEPTED
messages.note: The table allows this move for this actor. The customer can no longer cancel alone.

messages.label: assign(O-7, kitchen)
messages.note: Acceptance triggers rider search. The order keeps moving while the search runs.

messages.label: offer to R1 (nearest)
messages.note: Free riders within range are ranked by distance. The nearest gets the first offer.

messages.label: R1 declines
messages.note: A decline is expected. The assigner moves to the next rider in the ranking.

messages.label: offer to R2
messages.note: The second offer goes out. The offer count is capped so the order is not stuck.

messages.label: R2 reserved
messages.note: `take` removes R2 from the free pool atomically, so no other order gets R2.

messages.label: RESTAURANT: READY
messages.note: The kitchen moves the order through `PREPARING` to `READY`. Only the rider may pick it up.

messages.label: RIDER: PICKED_UP, DELIVERED
messages.note: The rider owns the last two moves. `DELIVERED` is terminal.

code.title: Lifecycle with owners
code.caption: The lifecycle is a table of allowed moves, each tagged with the actor who may make it.

walk.text: Statuses and actors are enums. A `Transition` record is a value, so `equals` compares all three fields.
The lifecycle reads like a spec. A product manager can check it line by line.
On a typo, `valueOf` throws as the class initialises, so first use fails loudly.
One gate checks status, target and actor together. The error names all three for support logs.
A late customer cancel and a restaurant marking pickup are both refused; the log stays clean.
Each accepted move records who did it. That audit trail settles refund disputes.

code.title: Rider offers with declines
code.caption: Nearest riders get offers in turn; declines move on, and an empty result queues the order.

walk.text: `R1` is nearest but declines every offer. `R3` is outside the 3 km radius.
The pool owns availability. `take` is an atomic check-and-remove, as in the cab matcher.
The constructor rejects a zero radius or zero offers before any order is processed.
Filter by radius, sort by distance then id, and cap how many riders are asked.
A decline moves to the next rider. Accepting still needs `take` to win the race.
An empty `Optional` means "retry later". The caller queues the order instead of throwing.

pitfalls: Checking only from and to, not the actor, lets a rider mark food ready or cancel.
Assigning a rider at `PLACED` wastes rider time when the restaurant then rejects the order.
Offering every rider at once makes several accept; offer in turn, or reserve atomically.

quiz.q: A fresh pool from the demo, but `maxOffers` is 1. What is O-7's result?
quiz.why: With one offer allowed, only the nearest rider, `R1`, is asked. `R1` declines, the loop ends, and the empty `Optional` becomes the fallback text.

takeaway: Every lifecycle move has an owner; rider offers go nearest first, in turn.

starters: Where should the retry queue for unassigned orders live?
How do I stop an order from waiting forever if no rider ever accepts?
Should rider assignment use the Observer pattern on the ACCEPTED status?
